campaign.title: Our Campaign
campaign.subtitle: The adventures of a party that should probably not be trusted with anything.

party.name: Alexander Warden
party.description: Alexander Warden is a protector of truth and the weak. Part Harpy Eagle

log.text: Took point on negotiations with the tavern owner and the ship's quartermaster, securing free (unpaid) passage for the whole crew. Overperformed at cargo-hauling thanks to his 20 strength, yanking other sailors off their feet, and found a bloodstained cloth hidden in a cargo crate.

Loaded cargo, rigged sails, found the bloodstained cloth in a crate, handed out Ghalen's excellent cooking, tried to sneak a snack before lunch and got scolded, and accidentally shot the quartermaster Quart dead through a door after Phineas's loud knocking. Later knocked Gravestone out cold to keep him quiet and ended up holding one of the stolen heart fruits.

party.name: Ghalen Mordecai
party.description: Ghalen is our fearless captain that wears a wolf pelt. Part Painted Dog

log.text: Cast Good Berries and distributed them to the party, held onto Milo's share. Showed off his hand-drawn map, which got a waterway/boat route added by Calazar. Worked deck-scrubbing and kitchen duty aboard the ship.

Cooked an excellent lunch (nat 20), handed out rotten-food 'justice' to Skidmark and Butt Stuff for their harassment and threats, killed Fishfucker, and later helped harvest hearts from Forehead, Butt Stuff, Fishfucker, and Skidmark to replace the stolen heart fruits.

party.name: Phineas Fernspark
party.description: Phineas is our resident cleric who was raised in a cave cult. Part Caracal Cat

log.text: Revealed as the richest party member with 44 gold. Repeatedly angled toward robbing the bank, got caught staking it out and was dragged off by the ear. Later hid in cargo crates instead of helping load the ship.

Hid in cargo to dodge work, got weak-kneed over Ghalen's cooking, knocked loudly and annoyingly on the captain's door (leading to Quart's accidental death), then executed Forehead and Skidmark, blew out Gravestone's suicidal dynamite with Gust of Wind, and helped harvest the replacement hearts.

party.name: Milo Dozewell
party.description: Milo is our sleepyhead who hates his sister. Part Firefly

log.text: Absent the entire session (presumed overslept). Strongly implied, via bootprint evidence, to be the one who trashed the Tomoro tavern last time the party was there, though no one connected the dots on screen.
Slept through boarding and used a Firefly transformation charge to sneak aboard, got discovered hiding in a hammock, and later held Forehead down so Phineas could finish him off for his heart.

party.name: Calazar Dorento
party.description: Calazar is our mute rogue with silent shotguns. Part Cuttlefish

log.text: Showed off his detailed hand-drawn map, which everyone else was politely obsessed with over Ghalen's. Handled ship rigging duties post-boarding, and smudged a contract detail with dockside water while making a dramatic entrance.

Investigated the marked cargo crate and found four stolen heart fruits, decapitated Butt Stuff, and later Wild Shaped into a cuttlefish to sneak into the locked captain's quarters, finding documents proving the ship is deliberately sailing to the Rat Folk Kingdom instead of the party's destination.
Reluctantly agreed to take the whole party on as free crew after they signed an unpaid labor contract; promptly fired four veteran sailors to make room for them.
Held Alexander at gunpoint after his tavern was ransacked, and banned the party from returning unless they find the real culprit.
Glimpsed briefly at a distance near the helmsman, face shadowed by a large hat; not yet approached.

npcs.name: Captain Fishbone

log.text: Finally introduced himself after enjoying Ghalen's cooking (19/20). Remained suspicious of the string of crew deaths but mostly shrugged them off as long as the cargo still gets delivered. His quarters were secretly searched by Calazar.

npcs.description: The ship's secretive captain, always concealed by a coat and cavalier hat. Oddly particular about the fish he eats and entirely unbothered by his crew dying around him.

npcs.name: Quart

log.text: Accidentally shot through the captain's quarters door by Alexander after Phineas's loud, annoying knocking. Thrown overboard by Phineas and Gravestone.

npcs.description: The ship's quartermaster, in charge of the labor contract, crew discipline, and cargo oversight.

npcs.name: Forehead

log.text: Held down by Milo and finished off by Phineas with an Eldritch Blast so his heart could be harvested as one of the four replacement hearts.

npcs.description: The ship's helmsman, and Quart's younger brother who briefly inherited the quartermaster role.

npcs.name: Gravestone

log.text: Mostly blind, helped throw Quart's body overboard, then had a suicidal frenzy after the murders started, lighting a stick of dynamite before Phineas blew it out with Gust of Wind. Was knocked unconscious by Alexander to keep him quiet.

npcs.description: Elderly halfling gunner in charge of the ship's cannons.

npcs.name: Hairbrush

log.text: Too scared and distracted to notice the murders happening around him; got forced to take the ship's wheel by the captain mid-crisis.

npcs.description: The newest crew recruit, only a week into sailing, searching for his long-lost fiancee who was lost at sea.

npcs.name: Skidmark

log.text: Fed rotten food in retaliation for threatening Phineas, passed out drunk during the chaos, and was ultimately killed by Phineas so his heart could be harvested as one of the four replacement hearts.

npcs.description: A drunk, foul-smelling crewmate who pulled a gun on Phineas as a 'prank' and was generally unpleasant.

npcs.name: Butt Stuff

log.text: Decapitated by Calazar; his heart was later harvested to replace one of the stolen fruit.

npcs.description: A crewmate below decks who flirted with and tried to kiss Alexander.

log.text: Fed rotten food but suffered no ill effects. Was later killed by Ghalen during the chaos below deck so his heart could be harvested.

quests.name: Reach the Uncharted Landmass

log.text: The party abandoned overland travel and bank/boat theft plans, ultimately signing on as unpaid ship labor to find passage there, though the ship's actual destination is unconfirmed.

The party boarded the merchant ship Copper Tide to reach their destination, but Calazar discovered documents proving the ship is actually sailing toward the Rat Folk Kingdom - not where the party intended to go. They have about two hours before passing the point of no return to redirect the ship.

quests.description: A new unnamed area appeared on the map overnight; the party is trying to reach it.

quests.name: Clear the Party's Name in Tomoro

log.text: The tavern owner refused the party service or help until they prove they didn't do it - complicated by the fact that Milo probably did.

quests.description: Find the real culprit behind the destroyed tavern in Tomoro to be allowed back into the village.

quests.name: Dispose of the Stolen Heart Fruits Discreetly

log.text: After finding four stolen 'heart fruit' in a marked cargo crate, the party took them and tried to cover their tracks by killing four crewmates (Forehead, Butt Stuff, Fishfucker, and Skidmark) to harvest replacement hearts of matching weight, hiding the bodies in hammocks to dump overboard once the ship docks.

mysteries.title: What happened to the Tomoro tavern?

clues.text: Bootprints found at the scene matched Milo's general size and gait, though no party member consciously connected this in-game.

mysteries.description: The Tomoro tavern was ransacked, allegedly by an animal.

mysteries.title: What's inside the bloodstained cargo crate?

clues.text: The cloth resembled a protective wrap used to keep something safe during transport; Alexander marked the crate to investigate further at night.

mysteries.resolution: The crate contained four carefully wrapped, still-beating 'heart fruits' - rare and dangerous enough to start wars, tied to the Anomaly Island ritual that gave the party their animal-based powers.
mysteries.description: Alexander found a bloodstained cloth wrap hidden inside a sealed, leather-strapped cargo crate while loading the ship.

mysteries.title: Who is the ship's captain?

clues.text: The captain goes by Captain Fishbone, always wears a face-concealing coat and hat, seems unfazed by multiple crew deaths, and is secretly steering the ship toward the Rat Folk Kingdom according to documents found in his quarters.

mysteries.description: A large, intimidating captain was seen briefly near the helmsman, face obscured by a wide-brimmed hat.

mysteries.title: Why is the ship really sailing to the Rat Folk Kingdom?
mysteries.description: Calazar found documents suggesting this specific ship and its cargo run (the heart fruits) were deliberately sought out, with the true destination being the Rat Folk Kingdom rather than where the party wanted to go.

loot.description: Distributed by Ghalen to the party (two each), with Milo's portion held onto by Ghalen.
Signed agreement granting the party free passage on the merchant ship in exchange for labor; a stray water drop smudged a key detail (compensation or employment length).

Freshly cut, still-beating fruits tied to the Anomaly Island ritual. Deadly to anyone who isn't an Anomaly survivor or doesn't match the fruit's 'animal type.' Hidden among the party after replacing them with harvested crew hearts.

loot.item: Documents on the ship's true destination
loot.description: Papers found in the captain's quarters proving the ship was specifically sought out for its cargo run and is secretly headed to the Rat Folk Kingdom.

quotes.speaker: Calazar
quotes.text: We disguise ourselves and then we go outside and find a place where they trade money for goods and services and we take all the money.

quotes.speaker: Tavern Owner
quotes.text: You guys are not welcome here.

quotes.speaker: Alexander
quotes.text: Alexander Warden, protector of the people... We only need travel. No compensation is required.

quotes.speaker: DM
quotes.text: Be careful hiding under large cargo - cargo can shift while the boat is on the water.

quotes.speaker: Alexander
quotes.text: Everything you see here is on me.

quotes.speaker: Captain Fishbone
quotes.text: I don't know this crew, but most of you seem quite incompetent. At least we have a good cook.

quotes.speaker: DM
quotes.text: A loud gunshot goes off through the door. Luckily he didn't know how tall you were. You shot right over your head and killed the quartermaster.

quotes.speaker: Milo
quotes.text: What am I gonna do with the heart?

sessions.title: Signed, Sealed, and Underpaid
sessions.summary: The party abandons a plan to walk two days to a mysterious new landmass, gets kicked out of a village they may have accidentally traumatized, and ends up signing an unpaid labor contract just to get a boat ride.
recap: The party gathered after a long rest in Port Plywood, having noticed a strange new unnamed area appear on the map overnight. With Milo mysteriously absent (presumed asleep, possibly dead - nobody checked too hard), the group debated how to reach the far side of the island, since Calazar's shiny new hand-drawn map showed no direct route by land or sea.

Ideas ranged from the practical (hitchhiking, buying a boat) to the deeply impractical (robbing a bank, staging a mutiny to steal a ship). Phineas in particular could not let go of the bank heist idea, going so far as to "scout" the bank in person, use its bathroom, and then get caught staring at it suspiciously before Alexander physically dragged him away by the ear.

The party settled on traveling to the town of Tomoro (formerly 'Tomorrow,' renamed by the DM to save map space) to try to borrow horses and a carriage. Unfortunately, Tomoro remembered them: last time the party visited, Phineas (in cat form at the time) had convinced the town he was a murderer via a catastrophically bad deception roll, and the townsfolk had watched them clean up a bar fight while keeping a terrified distance the whole time.

Arriving in Tomoro, the party found villagers cleaning up a destroyed tavern - the actual culprit was Milo, though nobody present recognized his bootprints as his despite a strong investigation roll. The tavern owner, at gunpoint-negotiating distance, made clear the party was not welcome back unless they found the real culprit, and did not appreciate Calazar's insistence that 'not all four' of them were criminals.

With Tomoro closed to them and no horses forthcoming, the party pivoted (again) to the shipyard, using Calazar's map to identify a possible sea route. None of the five ships on offer were remotely affordable, so the party leaned into being 'mercenaries' and instead negotiated free passage in exchange for labor - Alexander handling negotiations while flexing his 20 strength and general obliviousness to how contracts work.

The quartermaster had everyone sign an employment agreement with zero compensation and an unspecified end date. A stray drop of water from Calazar's dramatic dockside entrance smudged the contract's crucial details, though it's unclear if this will matter later. The signed sailors immediately replaced a group of four unhappy, presumably mutiny-planning veteran sailors, who were fired on the spot and sent off looking bitter.

The party got to work: Alexander overperformed at hauling cargo (accidentally yanking other sailors off their feet), Calazar handled rigging like the sea elf he is, Galen scrubbed decks and cooked, and Phineas immediately found a hiding spot in the cargo crates and did essentially nothing.

While hauling boxes, Alexander noticed one crate was packed with a bloodstained cloth wrap hidden among the cargo. He tugged it partway out before it caught resistance, marked the crate with a notch to identify it later, and decided to investigate further at night - a loose thread the party may want to pull on again.

As the ship set sail, the party caught a glimpse of an intimidating, shadow-faced captain standing near the helmsman, though nobody got close enough to learn anything more. The session ended with the ship pulling away from port, destination uncertain, cargo secrets unresolved, and the ominous DM-provided trailer tip: 'Be careful hiding under large cargo - cargo can shift while the boat is on the water.'
highlights: Phineas floated (and repeatedly circled back to) robbing the bank, culminating in him being dragged away by the ear mid-stakeout.
Phineas peed on the outside wall of the bank after a 'roll for luck,' getting the worst possible roll.
Alexander tried to kneel apologetically in front of a terrified villager sweeping glass, rolled a natural 20 to avoid the glass with his knee, only for her to have already fled in terror.
The tavern owner held Alexander at gunpoint over the ransacked bar - actually Milo's doing - while the party bickered over whether 'all four' of them were criminals.
Alexander negotiated an unpaid labor contract for the whole party while insisting they needed 'no compensation,' shushing Galen when he tried to ask about pay.
Alexander's 20 strength turned cargo-hauling into a hazard, yanking other sailors clean off their feet.
Phineas immediately abandoned all responsibility and hid inside the ship's cargo crates for the whole loading sequence.
Alexander discovered a bloodstained cloth hidden inside a sealed cargo crate and marked it to investigate later.
decisions: Abandoned plans to walk two days, rob a bank, or steal a ship outright.
Chose not to seek help from Tomoro after learning the town feared and distrusted them.
Signed an unpaid labor contract to secure free passage on a merchant ship rather than paying for one.
Alexander decided not to immediately report or fully investigate the bloody cloth found in the cargo, planning to return to it later.
sessions.cliffhanger: The ship has set sail toward parts unknown with a mysterious blood-stained item hidden in the cargo hold, an intimidatingly shadow-faced captain nobody's spoken to yet, and a warning that cargo can shift dangerously at sea - right where Phineas is hiding.
sessions.in_game_days: About half a day, ending with the ship's departure
table_talk: Extended tangent about robbing convenience stores vs. banks vs. 'the Guild.'
Debate over whether Good Berries look like angry cherry bombs from Plants vs. Zombies or homies from Big Mom's feast in One Piece.
Long derail about the party's earlier brothel visit, terrible attractiveness rolls, and someone allegedly getting syphilis in the bath.
DM's saga of accidentally hitting the Discord map update button and revealing spoiler place names.
Riffing on Calazar's ink-cloud ability being useless outside water and just making him an obvious paint bomb.
Random tangent about Rocket League boost mechanics applied to Calazar's underwater ink ability.
Off-topic chat about Cores Light beer cheese Pringles and blue raspberry candy.
Joke about the fired sailors being 'about to level up' and get a mutiny pension before getting canned.

sessions.title: Hearts, Shotguns, and Skidmark's Diaper
sessions.summary: The party boarded their new merchant ship, met the worst crew in the world, and by lunchtime had accidentally (and then not-so-accidentally) murdered most of it while stealing four mysterious beating hearts from the cargo hold.
recap: The session opened with everyone settling into their forced labor contract aboard the merchant ship: Phineas hid in the cargo to avoid work, Ghalen scrubbed decks and helped in the kitchen, Alexander loaded cargo and rigged sails, and Calazar worked the rigging near the crow's nest. Milo, true to form, had overslept and used a charge of his Firefly transformation just to sneak aboard before departure, waking up in a crew hammock below deck like nothing happened.

While loading cargo, Alexander found a blood-stained cloth hidden in one of the crates and marked it for later investigation. The quartermaster, a burly red-haired man named Quart, sent away four paid crewmates to make room for the party's free labor, and Alexander tried and failed to memorize their faces (rolled too low, remembered just one). The ship's actual captain stayed hidden in his quarters the entire time, wearing a coat and hat that concealed his face - nobody got so much as a clear look at him before he vanished below deck.

The crew turned out to be, charitably, a lot: a nervous mute deckhand the party nicknamed Fishfucker, a drunk old-timer named Skidmark who pulled a gun on Phineas as a 'mercenary prank,' a helmsman called Forehead, an elderly halfling gunner named Gravestone, a rookie named Hairbrush searching for his long-lost fiancee, and a crewmate downstairs named Butt Stuff who flirted with and tried to kiss Alexander. Calazar, in a fit of professional courtesy, advised Alexander to 'use protection' by nodding at his shotgun.

Ghalen cooked lunch (rolled a 20) and the crew loved it, with Alexander handing out the good plates while the captain - who introduced himself as Captain Fishbone - was oddly cagey about the fish in the meal. Ghalen decided the crew's various offenses (Skidmark's gun stunt, Butt Stuff's unwanted advances) warranted consequences, and spiked Skidmark's and Butt Stuff's plates with rotten food instead of poison. Skidmark passed out drunk; Butt Stuff ate his tainted meal with no ill effects whatsoever. Alexander, for his part, tried to sneak a snack before lunch and got scolded for it.

Calazar, sent by Alexander to investigate the marked crate, pried it open to reveal four freshly cut, still-beating 'heart fruits' - virgin, unbitten, and apparently valuable enough to start wars. The party determined these related to the Anomaly Island ritual that gave them their animal-based powers, and that eating one not matching your type would kill a normal person outright. They agreed the fruits were too dangerous to leave on the ship, but needed to replace the stolen hearts' weight and hide the theft from the captain.

Things escalated fast. Phineas knocked loudly and annoyingly on the captain's door trying to get his attention, and Alexander's shot went clean through the door and through Quart's skull instead, killing the quartermaster instantly. Blaming it on 'Fishfucker' via deception didn't stick with the suspicious captain, who instead had the party haul him down to find the real culprit - only to discover Butt Stuff already decapitated by Calazar. The captain, increasingly done with his own crew, started treating the mounting body count as just Tuesday.

With hearts needed to replace the stolen fruit, the party turned predatory: Milo held Forehead (who turned out to be Quart's younger brother, conveniently inheriting the dead quartermaster's position moments before dying) down while Phineas finished him with an Eldritch Blast to the back of the head, splattering blood everywhere. Phineas also killed Skidmark, and Ghalen killed Fishfucker. The explosion sent Gravestone - already blind and pushed over the edge by the chaos - into a suicidal frenzy; he lit a stick of dynamite, only for Phineas to blow it out with Gust of Wind before it could go off. Alexander then knocked Gravestone out cold to keep him quiet. Phineas and Ghalen harvested the hearts from Forehead, Butt Stuff, Fishfucker, and Skidmark to replace the four stolen fruit.

The party scrambled to hide the evidence: bodies stuffed into hammocks disguised as sleeping crew, blood and mess hastily mopped, and the plan settled on dumping the corpses overboard once the ship docked rather than risk it now. Meanwhile Calazar, having slipped into the locked captain's quarters in cuttlefish form via Wild Shape, searched Fishbone's cabin and found documents proving this ship and its cargo run were specifically sought out - and that its current course leads straight to the Rat Folk Kingdom, not the party's intended destination.

With the ship nearing the point of no return (about two hours out from a course correction being possible), the party was left scrambling for a plan: convince Hairbrush to alter course, force the issue by disabling the ship, or some combination of mutiny and improvisation. No firm plan was settled before the session ended, leaving the party with four stolen heart fruits, three crew corpses hidden in hammocks, an unmet and increasingly suspicious captain, and a ship sailing toward entirely the wrong kingdom.
highlights: Ghalen rolled a natural 20 cooking lunch and genuinely impressed the murderous ship's captain with his cuisine.
Phineas face-planted down the stairs from an 18 Charisma save after smelling the food too hard, while Alexander got scolded for trying to sneak a snack before lunch.
Phineas's overly loud, annoying knock on the captain's door led to Alexander accidentally shooting the quartermaster Quart clean through it, instantly creating the session's first murder mystery.
Milo held Forehead down while Phineas executed him with an Eldritch Blast to the back of the head - and the captain and most of the crew failed their perception checks to notice an exploding man.

Gravestone, pushed past his limit by the chaos, lit a stick of dynamite in a suicidal frenzy; Phineas blew it out with Gust of Wind just in time to avert a ship-wide explosion. Alexander then knocked him out cold.
Fishfucker survived eating rotten poisoned fish completely unscathed, to everyone's bafflement, before Ghalen finished him off anyway.
Calazar turned into a cuttlefish to escape the locked captain's quarters, where he uncovered that the ship was deliberately steering toward the Rat Folk Kingdom.
sessions.cliffhanger: With three crew corpses stuffed in hammocks, four stolen heart fruits in their bags, and proof the ship is secretly bound for the Rat Folk Kingdom instead of their destination, the party has about two hours before the ship passes the point of no return - and still no plan beyond vague talk of mutiny, sabotage, or just asking Hairbrush nicely.
